original_question: Let G be a profinite group with fewer than 2ℵ0 conjugacy classes of elements of infinite order. Must G be a torsion group? This holds in the case when G is finitely generated(J. S. Wilson, Arch. Math., 120(2023), 557–563). John
target_in_paper: Problem 21.136 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": it asks whether a profinite group with fewer than 2^{ℵ_0} conjugacy classes of elements of infinite order must be a torsion group, and it notes that the finitely generated case is known by Wilson (2023).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost exactly: it has the correct ambient object (a profinite group G), the correct hypothesis (fewer than 2^{ℵ_0} conjugacy classes of elements of infinite order), the correct conclusion under discussion (whether G must be torsion), and the same background note that the finitely generated case is known.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the objects being counted should be stated explicitly as the G-conjugacy classes x^G of elements x in G having infinite order.
The cardinality condition should be written explicitly as 'strictly less than 2^{ℵ_0}', i.e. fewer than continuum many such conjugacy classes.
The term 'torsion group' should be unpacked as 'every element of G has finite order'.
It is worth saying explicitly that no finite-generation hypothesis is assumed in the question itself; finite generation appears only in the known special case mentioned afterward.
refined_question: Let G be a profinite group such that the set {x^G : x in G and x has infinite order} has cardinality strictly less than 2^{ℵ_0}. Must G be a torsion group, that is, must every element of G have finite order?
justification: The draft is essentially a restatement of the paper's exact numbered open problem. In this arXiv paper, which is a problem compendium rather than a theorem-proof article, the relevant target is Problem 21.136, and the sentence about the finitely generated case is part of the problem's own accompanying comment. There is no narrower neighboring formulation in the local context that should replace it, so the right refinement is only to make the counting condition and the meaning of 'torsion' explicit while keeping the scope unchanged.
